data.raw_text:
Tropical Depression 23W (Mirasol) has just emerged in the South China Sea, and convection has started to refire around its circulation. For context, 23W unofficially peaked as a high-end tropical storm yesterday around 16th 18z. The storm developed much faster than expected, with radar showing a well-defined eyewall before landfall in Casiguran, Aurora, Philippines. Hopefully, everyone stayed safe, and the impacts were not too bad there.

23W will face moderate westerly upper-level wind shear for the next 24 hours, as depicted below in the GFS loop. However, wind shear is expected to subside. The storm will continue heading northwest and is forecast to have an approximate 24-hour window to intensify in a relatively favorable environment. Although some dry air may sneak in, it is not a major concern for the storm. 23W will probably peak as a high-end tropical storm or briefly a Category 1 typhoon when it nears landfall east of Hong Kong. Flooding and rough swells are the primary concerns, and residents should start preparing for such impacts as soon as possible.
